title: Maximum Earnings From Taxi
statement:
A taxi travels along a road whose points are numbered `1` to `n`, starting at point `1` and moving only toward higher-numbered points. Each entry `rides[i] = [start_i, end_i, tip_i]` is a passenger who wants to be taken from point `start_i` to point `end_i` and will tip `tip_i` dollars; carrying that passenger earns `end_i - start_i + tip_i` dollars.

The taxi holds at most one passenger at any moment, though one passenger may be dropped off and another picked up at the very same point. Choose which passengers to carry so that the total amount earned is as large as possible, and return that total.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every set of compatible rides is exponential. But the taxi only moves forward, so the best total on reaching a point depends only on the best totals at earlier points. Let `dp[point]` be the most money you can hold when the taxi stands at `point`. Either you arrived without a passenger on the last stretch, keeping `dp[point - 1]`, or some ride ended right here, adding its earning to whatever you had at its start.

## Approach

1. Bucket the rides by drop-off point: `endingAt[end]` holds `[start, earning]` with `earning = end - start + tip`.
2. Fill `dp` with zeros; `dp[1]` stays `0` because nothing can end at point 1.
3. For each `point` from 2 to `n`, start from `dp[point - 1]` (drive empty for one step).
4. For each ride ending at `point`, try `dp[start] + earning` and keep the larger value.
5. Return `dp[n]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 5`, rides `[2,5,4]` and `[1,5,1]` both end at 5, with earnings `5 - 2 + 4 = 7` and `5 - 1 + 1 = 5`. Points 2 to 4 have no endings, so `dp` stays `0` through point 4. At point 5, `dp[5]` starts at `0`, becomes `dp[2] + 7 = 7`, and `dp[1] + 5 = 5` does not beat it. The answer is `7`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m) for `m` rides: each point is visited once and each ride is tried once.
- Space: O(n + m) for `dp` and the buckets.

## Pitfalls

- Drop-off and pick-up may share a point, so a ride starting at `start` may use `dp[start]` itself, not `dp[start - 1]`.
- Forgetting `dp[point] = dp[point - 1]` loses earnings from rides that ended earlier.
- The total can exceed 2^31 (many rides with tips near 10^5), so Java and C need a 64-bit result.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `endingAt` | for each drop-off point, the rides ending there as `[start, earning]` |
| `dp` | `dp[point]` is the best total on reaching `point` |
| `point` | the point being filled |
| `start`, `earning` | a ride's pick-up point and what it pays |

narration.2: Make an empty bucket for every point so rides can be grouped by where they end.
narration.4: File the ride under its drop-off point with its full earning, distance plus tip.
narration.6: dp[point] will be the most money you can have when the taxi reaches point; nothing is earned at point 1.
narration.7: Fill the points in driving order, from 2 up to n.
narration.8: Driving the last step empty keeps everything earned by the previous point.
narration.9: Consider every ride that drops its passenger exactly here.
narration.10: Taking it adds its earning to the best total at its pick-up point.
narration.13: The best total on reaching the last point is the answer.
